title: The Dockmaster's Watch
logline: A retiring dockmaster hires a pilot to courier her handwritten black-berth ledger to a quiet buyer before station administration impounds her final severance package.

roles.description: Forty years managing orbital intake slips; arthritic, cynical, trying to secure enough retirement scrip to live off-station.
The financial administrator reviewing all executive retirements to claw back unbonded severance pay.
A discreet archivist who buys private station memoirs and unlogged berth diaries for wealthy collectors.
The station security brigade monitoring outgoing baggage and executive departures.
A dingy observation cubicle suspended over the primary freighter docking bay.
The passenger concourse where retired station staff wait for outbound passenger lighters.

public_situation: {role:retiring_dockmaster} cleans out her locker above the main docking bay as {role:station_comptroller} conducts a mandatory pre-retirement asset review.
private_truth: The dockmaster's personal pocket ledger records forty years of off-the-books docking fees she allowed old retired smugglers to pay directly to her personal emergency fund.

beats.public_change: Notice boards post the dockmaster's ceremonial retirement banquet while constables begin auditing terminal archive logs.

missions.reason: She needs an outside pilot to purchase an unmonitored encrypted data slate from the exchange and deliver it to her office before security monitors her terminal.
missions.private_fact: She is transcribing forty years of off-ledger berth records onto the slate before her municipal console access is permanently revoked.

beats.public_change: {role:dock_constabulary} establishes biometric scanning portals across {role:transit_lounge}, screening all departing senior personnel.

missions.reason: She needs a pilot to scan the transit lounge passenger scanner net to locate the quiet collector without alerting the constabulary checkpoint.
missions.private_fact: The comptroller has placed a covert trace on her biometric token to seize the notebook before she boards the passenger shuttle.

beats.public_change: The final boarding siren echoes through {role:transit_lounge} as luggage conveyors load the outbound orbital shuttle.

missions.reason: She asks the pilot to courier the sealed data slate directly into the hands of the quiet collector before the final departure horn sounds.
missions.private_fact: The slate contains proof that several prominent retired merchants built their fortunes on uninspected contraband berths she approved.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot stands between the waiting collector and the approaching comptroller at the passenger gate.

options.label: Hand the slate to the quiet collector to fund the dockmaster's retirement
Surrender the ledger to the comptroller for a municipal recovery fee
Wipe the data slate to protect the retired smugglers from exposure

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot delivers the encrypted ledger to the collector.
resolutions.summary: The collector pays the agreed scrip. {role:retiring_dockmaster} boards the passenger lighter with a secure pension, leaving station management with empty files.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot slipped forty years of handwritten docking secrets to an off-world collector so a tired dockmaster could retire.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot surrenders the slate to the station comptroller.
resolutions.summary: The comptroller seizes the ledger. {role:retiring_dockmaster} is stripped of severance, while {role:dock_constabulary} begins blackmailing retired merchants across {system}.

consequences.public_summary: Dockworkers grumble that a hired courier turned over the retiring dockmaster's private records to station auditors for a payout.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot wipes the memory core before handing over the casing.
resolutions.summary: The slate is erased. Old retired smugglers breathe easy, {role:retiring_dockmaster} departs on basic municipal relief scrip, and the comptroller finds no proof.

resolutions.reached_by: The courier is aborted or security checkpoints intercept the slate.
resolutions.summary: Constabulary monitors detect the transfer and impound the dockmaster's luggage. The ledger is confiscated, and {role:retiring_dockmaster} is evicted into station public housing.

loose_threads.detail: The slate case contains three paper docking receipts dated thirty years ago stamped with a decommissioned freight seal.
A personnel board bulletin lists a retroactive clawback policy applying to dock officials retiring within ninety days.
The quiet buyer holds an open-ended first-class passage coupon issued by a shipping line that went bankrupt a decade ago.

radio_hooks: Station administration announces retirement ceremony for forty-year veteran dockmaster.
Auditing commission introduces automated reconciliation procedures for historical berthing logs.
Passenger transit authority reminds departing residents to declare all proprietary data hardware.

voice_direction.retiring_dockmaster: Slow, raspy, and dismissive. Speaks of station directors as temporary annoyances and refers to docking rigs by forty-year-old decommissioned numbers.
voice_direction.station_comptroller: Smug, articulate, and patronizing. Frames predatory pension clawbacks as routine accounting tidiness and never raises his voice.
